audit_items.proof_trace: The canonical chain check (IsCanonical) at line 82 is performed once when creating the batcher, but the fork choice state can change during the multi-batch iteration loop (lines 97-110). During a reorganization between batches, blocks that were canonical when the batcher was created may become non-canonical, yet the batcher's cached canonicalFilter state (prevRoot) causes it to continue serving their data columns without re-checking canonicity.
audit_items.attack_scenario: An attacker triggers a fork choice reorganization (via strategic block/attestation timing) after the RPC handler creates the batcher but before all batches complete. The batcher then serves data columns from blocks that are no longer on the canonical chain, violating the invariant that all served sidecars must be from the current fork choice chain.
